name: CourtListener
summary: Free Law Project's US legal database: case law opinions, PACER dockets and filings, judges and oral arguments, with full-text search and citation lookup.

api_token.description: A CourtListener API token (free account, shown on your profile's API page). Sent as 'Authorization: Token <token>'.

notes: Default throttle for authenticated users: 5 requests per minute, 50 per hour, 125 per day, rolling windows, all applied at once. Use fields/omit to keep payloads small.

Filters are Django-style: field=value, field__gte / __lte / __gt / __lt / __range, related fields joined with __ (cluster__docket__court=scotus), and ! to negate (court__jurisdiction!=F). An OPTIONS request on an endpoint lists its filters and ordering fields.
A case's web URL carries the cluster id, not the opinion id; look a case up on clusters. Use cluster case names, not docket names.
Docket numbers are not unique; always add a court filter.

endpoints.name: Search case law, dockets, judges or oral arguments
endpoints.summary: Full-text search with highlighted snippets; type picks opinions, RECAP dockets/documents, judges or audio.

q.description: Query; supports field operators such as caseName:foo.

type.description: o case law (default), r dockets with up to 3 documents, rd RECAP documents, d dockets, p judges, oa oral arguments.

highlight.description: on to highlight matches; off by default.

semantic.description: true for semantic search (case law only).

notes: Pages with the cursor in the next URL. Counts for types d and r are approximate above 2,000.
Results are cached for ten minutes; for monitoring, the Alert API is preferred over polling.

endpoints.name: List opinion clusters
endpoints.summary: Cases (opinion clusters) filtered by docket, court, date and other fields.

order_by.description: Sort fields, comma-separated; prefix - for descending (OPTIONS lists the allowed ones).

fields.description: Only these fields, comma-separated; __ for nested fields.

page.description: Page number; at most 100 pages. Ordering by id, date_modified or date_created pages with the next/previous URLs instead.

count.description: on returns only the total count.

endpoints.name: Get an opinion cluster
endpoints.summary: One case: names, dates, citations, judges and links to its opinions.

endpoints.name: List opinions
endpoints.summary: Opinions filtered by cluster, court or docket fields.

order_by.description: Sort fields, comma-separated; prefix - for descending (OPTIONS lists the allowed ones).

fields.description: Only these fields, comma-separated; __ for nested fields.

page.description: Page number; at most 100 pages. Ordering by id, date_modified or date_created pages with the next/previous URLs instead.

count.description: on returns only the total count.

endpoints.name: Get an opinion
endpoints.summary: One opinion's text (html_with_citations is the most reliable field), type, author and the opinions it cites.

endpoints.name: List dockets
endpoints.summary: Dockets filtered by court, docket number and other fields.

order_by.description: Sort fields, comma-separated; prefix - for descending (OPTIONS lists the allowed ones).

fields.description: Only these fields, comma-separated; __ for nested fields.

page.description: Page number; at most 100 pages. Ordering by id, date_modified or date_created pages with the next/previous URLs instead.

count.description: on returns only the total count.

notes: Docket entries, parties and attorneys are not in docket responses.

endpoints.name: List courts

endpoints.name: Look up citations in text
endpoints.summary: Parses legal citations out of text (or one volume/reporter/page) and resolves them to clusters.

text.description: Text to parse, up to 64,000 characters.

volume.description: Volume of a single citation (with reporter and page).

notes: A read over POST, form-encoded. Up to 250 citations per request; 60 valid citations per minute, then 429 with a wait_util timestamp (field name as the docs spell it).
Statutes, law journals, id. and supra citations are not looked up.
